title: Histologically Validated Ex Vivo Characterization of Intraplaque Hemorrhage and Lipid Components Using Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Accurate characterization of carotid plaque components is essential for stroke risk assessment. Intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) is a well-established marker of plaque vulnerability, whereas lipid-rich necrotic cores (LRNCs) often show overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. The purpose of this study was to compare quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) with conventional MRI in differentiating IPH and lipid components in carotid plaques using ex vivo histologic validation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-four carotid plaque specimens obtained by en bloc excision during carotid endarterectomy between October 2017 and August 2021 were examined. All specimens underwent ex vivo MRI at 3T, including T1WI, T2WI, and TOF-equivalent FLASH, as well as QSM reconstructed from multiecho FLASH phase data. After MRI, specimens were serially sectioned and stained using H&E and immunohistochemical techniques. ROIs corresponding to histologically confirmed IPH and lipid components were delineated on MRI by consensus of 2 radiologists. On conventional MRI, signal intensities were measured in corresponding histologic regions, and contrast-to-noise ratios (CNRs) were calculated relative to surrounding agarose gel. On QSM, absolute magnetic susceptibility values were measured in the same regions. The difference between plaque tissue and the surrounding agarose gel was defined as the relative susceptibility value (rSV), which was used for statistical analysis. CNRs and rSVs among plaque components were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by the Steel-Dwass test for pair-wise comparisons. RESULTS: P P P Seventy-nine matched cross-sectional slices were analyzed, yielding 24 IPH, 61 LRNCs, and 13 foam-cell aggregates (FAs). No significant difference in CNR was observed between IPH and LRNC on T1WI or FLASH. Histopathologic analysis demonstrated that many LRNCs exhibited erythrocyte-derived remnants consistent with prior hemorrhagic events. FAs showed lower CNRs than IPH on T1WI and FLASH (< .05). On T2WI, IPH showed lower CNRs than LRNCs or FAs (< .05). On QSM, IPH demonstrated higher rSVs than LRNCs or FAs (< .01). CONCLUSIONS: Histologic validation demonstrates that many LRNCs contain erythrocyte remnants, which may contribute to their overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. QSM captures erythrocyte-derived susceptibility effects within plaques and provides complementary susceptibility-based information not available from conventional MRI.

The purpose of this study was to compare quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) with conventional MRI in differentiating IPH and lipid components in carotid plaques using ex vivo histologic validation.

title: Long-term graft and patient survival of patients with portal vein stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation; results from the multicenter multinational PORTAL registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) has become a standard treatment, but it is still burdened by complications such as portal vein stenosis (PVS). PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis after pLT. METHODS: Our study analyzed data from the Portal vein Obstruction Revascularisation Therapy After Liver transplantation (PORTAL) registry, which contains retrospective data from 21 centers, across 18 countries, over a 20-year period. Graft- and patient survival rates were determined after PVS diagnosis. RESULTS: This study included 239 patients (53% female; median age at pLT 1.1 years) diagnosed with PVS. The median age at diagnosis was 2.7 years. The overall ten-year graft survival was 90%, and the ten-year patient survival was 96%. One-year graft and patient survival was lowest in patients with PVS diagnosed ≤7 days after pLT (80% and 92%, respectively). Initial treatment strategies comprised of mostly endovascular procedures (87%), followed by conservative (11%) and surgical treatment (3%). Patient outcome did not differ between these treatment groups. Within the endovascular group, graft survival in patients treated with stent (n=26) was significantly lower compared to those with percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (n=181) (88% vs 98%, respectively, p=0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate excellent graft and patient survival after PVS diagnosis and its treatment. Further research is needed to determine the safety and efficacy of optimal management strategies, especially in early-onset PVS.

title: Adoption of Outpatient Management of Acute Low-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.
abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVE: To assess longitudinal outcomes of a multicomponent intervention designed to address key barriers to the outpatient management of low-risk pulmonary embolism (PE), and to define the most appropriate target population and metric for evaluating adoption. METHODS: We implemented a multicomponent intervention in the emergency department (ED) of a quaternary academic medical center. Outcomes were evaluated using the RE-AIM framework, comparing a 3-year preimplementation period (2016-2019) with active implementation (year I), postimplementation (year II), and maintenance (year III) periods. The primary outcome (adoption) was the proportion of low-PESI (≤85) patients discharged from the ED. Following implementation, the charts of all hospitalized low-PESI patients were reviewed to determine reasons for admission. RESULTS: Among 1,810 patients with acute PE, 705 (39.0%) had low-PESI scores. Adoption rose from 5.1% preimplementation to 16.1% (odds ratio [OR] 3.43, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.77 to 6.63), 24.0% (OR 5.98, 95% CI 3.04 to 11.78), and 33.3% (OR 9.24, 95% CI 5.04 to 16.92) in years I to III. There were no recurrent venous thromboembolism or deaths within 30 days of any ED discharge. Bleeding complications were rare (0%-4.3%) and none required hospitalization. Hospitalization decreased primarily among low-PESI patients without Hestia criteria, whereas admission of low-PESI Hestia-positive patients remained relatively constant. Excluding Hestia-positive cases, adoption increased from 9.0% preimplementation to 75% in the maintenance phase. CONCLUSION: In this single-center implementation study, a multicomponent intervention guided by RE-AIM resulted in a sustained increase in outpatient management of low-risk PE. Both the PESI score and Hestia criteria could be incorporated into the definition of the target population and future quality metrics.

title: Chronic Anticoagulation Increases Complications in Obliterative Prolapse Surgery.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Chronic anticoagulation has been identified as a risk factor for postoperative complications in other specialties, but there is a paucity of data on its effect on older women undergoing obliterative prolapse repair. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to assess whether chronic anticoagulation is associated with increased serious adverse events (SAEs) after obliterative prolapse surgery. STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort analysis of women 65 years or older undergoing obliterative prolapse repair at 2 academic institutions from 2016 to 2023. Patients were identified by Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) code and grouped by preoperative chronic anticoagulation status. The composite primary outcome was defined as SAE within 8 weeks of surgery. Multivariable logistic regression was performed, controlling for relevant variables with P <0.10 on univariate analysis. RESULTS: Among the 777 older women who underwent obliterative surgery, 97 (12.5%) were chronically anticoagulated. The most commonly used anticoagulants were apixaban (n = 37, 38.1%) and clopidogrel (n = 31, 32%), with 21.7% reporting concomitant use of aspirin. Anticoagulated individuals were more likely to be current smokers and to have a history of venous thromboembolism, myocardial infarction, and stroke (P < 0.05). Chronically anticoagulated women had 1.72 times greater adjusted odds of experiencing SAE (95% CI, 1.02-2.91). Chronic anticoagulation was associated with an increased incidence of readmission, cardiac complications, transfusion, hematoma, and organ-space surgical site infection (P < 0.05). Rates of SAEs were highest in individuals taking rivaroxaban (35.7%) and those taking concomitant aspirin (38.1%). CONCLUSIONS: Chronic anticoagulation is associated with increased odds of SAE in older women undergoing obliterative prolapse surgery. Physicians should consider this additional risk in surgical decision making and counseling on anticoagulant suspension and resumption perioperatively.

STUDY DESIGN: This was a retrospective cohort analysis of women 65 years or older undergoing obliterative prolapse repair at 2 academic institutions from 2016 to 2023.

title: Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy Prompting Diagnosis of Severe Aortic Regurgitation and Ascending Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: PURPOSE: To report a case of paracentral acute middle maculopathy (PAMM) in which persistent paracentral dysfunction prompted cardiovascular investigation and diagnosis of severe aortic regurgitation, reduced ejection fraction, and ascending aortic aneurysm. METHODS: Longitudinal ophthalmic assessment, multimodal retinal imaging, Humphrey SITA Central 10-2 testing, cardiovascular evaluation, surgical findings, histopathology, and targeted aortopathy genetic testing were reviewed. RESULTS: A 44-year-old man presented with intermittent right-eye visual disturbance and persistent paracentral scotoma after non-explanatory neuroimaging. Unaided visual acuity remained 20/25 (6/7.5; approximately 0.10 logMAR) in each eye, intraocular pressure was 16-19 mmHg, and anterior-segment examination was unremarkable. Multimodal imaging supported PAMM, with structural OCT inner retinal/inner nuclear layer involvement and qualitative OCT-A/fluorescein angiographic parafoveal perfusion compromise. The affected inner retinal/inner nuclear layer region decreased from 45 micrometres to 32 micrometres. Right-eye Humphrey SITA Central 10-2 mean deviation worsened from -3.67 dB on 03 March 2020 to -5.19 dB in February 2026 despite unchanged central acuity. Cardiovascular assessment revealed a 5.5-cm ascending aortic aneurysm, severe aortic regurgitation, and left-ventricular ejection fraction of 49%. The patient underwent elective Bentall procedure, with postoperative ejection-fraction improvement to 55%. No postoperative quantitative OCT-A reperfusion claim is made. CONCLUSION: PAMM may warrant systemic cardiovascular assessment when ocular findings do not fully explain persistent paracentral dysfunction. This case supports cautious multidisciplinary evaluation while avoiding unsupported claims of causality, quantitative OCT-A perfusion deficit, or postoperative retinal reperfusion.

RESULTS: A 44-year-old man presented with intermittent right-eye visual disturbance and persistent paracentral scotoma after non-explanatory neuroimaging.

title: Implementation of a multi-disciplinary hemodialysis access clinic improves time to surgical evaluation and access case volume.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Delays in hemodialysis access creation contribute to prolonged tunneled dialysis catheter dependence and morbidity. In March 2025, our institution implemented a multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic with weekly reserved appointments, same-day duplex vein mapping, and streamlined nephrology-to-surgery referral. We evaluated its effect on access volume, timing to surgical evaluation, and catheter dependence. METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review of adults undergoing hemodialysis access procedures at a tertiary academic center from March 17, 2024 to March 13, 2026. Access volume was compared before and after implementation. Patient-level timing metrics were compared between patients evaluated in standard vascular surgery clinic versus multidisciplinary accelerated clinic. RESULTS: p p p p p p Mean monthly access volume increased from 3.08 ± 2.15 to 8.58 ± 3.00 cases after implementation, an increase of 5.5 cases per month ( < 0.001). Annual access volume increased from 37 to 103 cases ( < 0.001). Among 53 patients, 29 were evaluated in the standard clinic and 24 in the multidisciplinary clinic. Referral-to-clinic time decreased from 63.6 ± 47.7 to 41.0 ± 35.9 days ( = 0.01). Clinic-to-operation time did not differ significantly (21.8 ± 18.5 vs 27.1 ± 17.2 days; = 0.14). Overall referral-to-operation time decreased from 85.4 ± 51.5 to 68.2 ± 43.9 days but did not reach significance ( = 0.07). Catheter dependence was lower in the multidisciplinary cohort (29% vs 48%; OR 0.36, 95% CI 0.11-1.16). Same-day vein mapping was performed more frequently in the accelerated clinic cohort than in the standard clinic cohort (100% vs 51.7%, < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: A multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic increased procedural volume and shortened time to surgical evaluation. However, total time to access creation was not significantly reduced, suggesting that downstream operative capacity may remain an important barrier.

In March 2025, our institution implemented a multidisciplinary accelerated hemodialysis access clinic with weekly reserved appointments, same-day duplex vein mapping, and streamlined nephrology-to-surgery referral. We evaluated its effect on access volume, timing to surgical evaluation, and catheter dependence.

title: Comparison of arteriovenous fistula patency in lipoprotein apheresis and haemodialysis: A matched case-control study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Arteriovenous fistulas constitute an effective vascular access option for haemodialysis, demonstrating high patency rates and lower infection risk compared with synthetic accesses. Treatment algorithms and patient characteristics differ between haemodialysis and apheresis therapy, and fistula outcomes in patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis have not yet been systematically evaluated. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study compared arteriovenous fistula outcomes in 29 patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis with those of 87 frequency-matched patients on haemodialysis. Matching criteria included age, sex, fistula configuration and diabetes mellitus status. Primary and secondary patency rates and associated risk factors were assessed over a 24-month follow-up period using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: n n n n p p p p The study included patients with radiocephalic ( = 72) or brachiocephalic ( = 44) arteriovenous fistulas. Indications for apheresis were elevated lipoprotein(a) levels ( = 26) and dyslipoproteinemia ( = 3). Mean age was comparable between groups (61.4 vs 61.2 years), as was the proportion of male patients (58.6% vs 60.9%). Diabetes mellitus was present in 58.6% of apheresis patients and 49.4% of haemodialysis patients. Two-year primary patency rates were comparable between groups (49.2% vs 50.8%), while secondary patency was lower in the apheresis group (59.9% vs 71.1%). In the apheresis cohort, diabetes was associated with reduced primary (HR, 4.034; 95 % CI, 1.10-14.80; = 0.035) and secondary patency (HR, 9.807; 95 % CI, 1.24-77.59; = 0.030). Apheresis before fistula creation demonstrated improved secondary patency (HR, 0.198; 95% CI, 0.04-0.94; = 0.042). In haemodialysis patients, hyperlipoproteinemia was associated with reduced secondary patency (HR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.01-5.14; = 0.046). CONCLUSIONS: Arteriovenous fistula patency in patients undergoing apheresis was comparable to haemodialysis patients despite elevated lipoprotein levels. Diabetes was associated with reduced fistula patency in lipoprotein apheresis. The findings support arteriovenous fistulas as long-term access option and highlight the importance of individualised access planning.

Treatment algorithms and patient characteristics differ between haemodialysis and apheresis therapy, and fistula outcomes in patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis have not yet been systematically evaluated. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective cohort study compared arteriovenous fistula outcomes in 29 patients receiving lipoprotein apheresis with those of 87 frequency-matched patients on haemodialysis.

title: Single-stage aneurysmorrhaphy, downstream venous plication and external PTFE reinforcement for multiple true aneurysms in a high-flow brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula: A case report.
abstract: True aneurysms of a haemodialysis arteriovenous fistula (AVF) and a co-existent high-flow state pose a particular surgical problem, because the structural and the haemodynamic abnormality must be corrected at the same operation if a precious native access is to be preserved. We report a 51-year-old woman maintained on thrice-weekly haemodialysis through an 18-month-old left brachiocephalic AVF, who developed two cephalic-vein true aneurysms (2.48 and 2.14 cm) in the outflow segment with an access flow of 6.7 L/min,(peak-systolic-velocity-based duplex estimate).concentric left-ventricular hypertrophy and grade 3 diastolic dysfunction Through a single incision we performed partial-wall aneurysmorrhaphy of both sacs, deliberate downstream venous plication for flow reduction, and circumferential external polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) reinforcement of the entire repaired and plicated segment, with intraoperative duplex titration of the haemodynamic endpoint. Access flow fell from 6.7 to 1.4 L/min (≈79% reduction) with preserved patency. The combined approach delivers structural repair, mechanical reinforcement and flow modulation in one stage and avoids prosthetic interposition, separate arterial dissection and prolonged catheter dependence.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy Is Associated With Lower Risk of Lower Extremity Amputation in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes and Foot Ulcer Without Coded Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Hypothesis-Generating Real-World Cohort Study.
abstract: AIMS: To compare lower extremity amputation (LEA) risk in adults with Type 2 diabetes and diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) treated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) versus other glucose-lowering therapy, and to test whether coded peripheral arterial disease (PAD) modifies this association and replicates across comparator classes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This new-user, active-comparator retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (queried 11 July 2026). Adults with Type 2 diabetes and DFU were propensity-score matched 1:1 on 22 covariates, giving 21 325 pairs for the primary comparison. Effect modification by coded PAD (ICD-10 I70.2) was examined in independently matched subgroups. Six sensitivity analyses were pre-specified: 30- and 180-day landmarks, all-cause mortality, background-therapy balancing, limb-severity adjustment and a broadened PAD definition. RESULTS: GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower 5-year LEA risk than all non-GLP-1 RA therapy (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.54-0.67). The association was confined to the no-PAD stratum (HR: 0.21, 0.13-0.33) and absent where PAD was coded (HR: 0.97, 0.78-1.20); ratio of hazard ratios 0.21 (0.13-0.36; p < 0.001). All-cause mortality was also lower (HR: 0.48, 0.45-0.50). The insulin no-PAD estimate persisted under background-therapy balancing (0.14), limb-severity adjustment (0.16) and 30- and 180-day landmarks (0.28, 0.33). Broadening the PAD definition attenuated the no-PAD association without abolishing it (HR: 0.34, 0.17-0.65). CONCLUSIONS: In Type 2 diabetes with DFU, GLP-1 RA use was associated with lower LEA risk, surviving six pre-specified sensitivity analyses. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This new-user, active-comparator retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network (queried 11 July 2026). Adults with Type 2 diabetes and DFU were propensity-score matched 1:1 on 22 covariates, giving 21 325 pairs for the primary comparison.

title: It Is Possible to Save the Kidney With Renal Artery Occlusion Without Autotransplantation: A Case Report.
abstract: Renal artery stenosis is a rare but important cause of renovascular hypertension in children that may lead to malignant hypertension and renal failure. A 13-year-old girl presented with malignant hypertension and acute kidney injury, and imaging demonstrated occlusion of both renal arteries. Endovascular recanalization was unsuccessful because of complete, heavily fibrotic occlusions involving a long segment of the right renal artery extending to the hilum, leaving no suitable distal artery for reconstruction, and a 7.3-mm segment of the left renal artery at its aortic origin. To preserve renal function, surgical revascularization was performed by in situ reimplantation of the left renal artery into the aorta, without autotransplantation. Postoperatively, renal function recovered, the proteinuria present at admission regressed, and the patient became normotensive without antihypertensive medication.

title: Incidentally Diagnosed Pulmonary Embolism Two Months After Living Liver Donation in a Donor With Homozygous MTHFR A1298C Mutation: A Case Report.
abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is widely performed in countries with limited cadaveric organ donation. Although donor hepatectomy is generally safe, venous thromboembolic events such as pulmonary embolism (PE) remain rare but potentially life-threatening complications. Genetic thrombophilia, including methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) mutations, may contribute to thrombotic risk. A 39-year-old female living liver donor underwent right donor hepatectomy for LDLT. The donor had no preoperative risk factors for venous thromboembolism, and a routine thrombophilia panel, including protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, and prothrombin gene mutations, was normal. Two months after surgery, an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan performed due to fluid collection adjacent to the remnant liver in ultrasound (USG) during routine follow-up incidentally revealed partial PE. Pulmonary CT angiography confirmed the finding, while lower extremity Doppler USG showed no evidence of deep vein thrombosis. Laboratory tests revealed elevated D-dimer and homocysteine levels. Further genetic evaluation demonstrated a homozygous MTHFR A1298C mutation. The patient was treated with low molecular weight heparin followed by oral anticoagulant therapy for 6 months, resulting in complete radiological resolution of the embolism. PE after donor hepatectomy is rare but potentially fatal. This case suggests that MTHFR A1298C mutation may represent a previously underrecognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism in living liver donors. In populations with a high prevalence of MTHFR mutations, extended thrombophilia screening and appropriate thromboprophylaxis may help reduce the risk of postoperative thromboembolic complications.

title: "Not so minor" - Digital Amputation as a precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish tertiary vascular centre.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for five-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality. METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017-2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry (HIPE) data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality. RESULTS: 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least one minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (± 12.7). 70% had PAD and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n=73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major re-amputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischaemic heart disease (IHD) (OR 2.796, 95% CI 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136) and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularisation at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8% and 48% at one, three and five years, respectively. CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

title: THE CLINICAL PROFILE OF RUPTURE: A 19-YEAR CASE-CONTROL STUDY OF ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSMS.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) presentation and quantify ruptures below current sex-specific elective repair thresholds. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study compared patients presenting with ruptured infrarenal AAA with a contemporaneous comparison group undergoing elective infrarenal AAA repair. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with ruptured presentation. The primary model included maximum aneurysm diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year; the extended model additionally included hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia. Discrimination was evaluated using optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC). RESULTS: Among 394 patients with infrarenal AAA, 194 presented with rupture and 200 underwent elective repair. Median diameter was 80.0 versus 53.0 mm (P < .001), and women comprised 10.9% versus 3.0% (P = .002), respectively. Diameter per 10-mm increase (odds ratio [OR], 2.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.84-2.61) and female sex (OR, 4.72; 95% CI, 1.49-14.94) were independently associated with ruptured presentation. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.836 for diameter alone, 0.832 for the primary model (diameter, age, female sex, and calendar year), and 0.840 for the extended model (primary model plus hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and dyslipidemia). Sixteen of 160 ruptures (10.0%) occurred below sex-specific thresholds. CONCLUSIONS: Diameter was the dominant factor associated with ruptured presentation, but female sex remained independently associated. These findings support diameter-based practice while highlighting the need for prospective, sex-aware, multiparametric risk assessment.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To identify factors associated with ruptured infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) presentation and quantify ruptures below current sex-specific elective repair thresholds. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study compared patients presenting with ruptured infrarenal AAA with a contemporaneous comparison group undergoing elective infrarenal AAA repair. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations with ruptured presentation.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Extracranial Carotid Artery Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare lesions managed by open surgical repair (OpR) or endovascular repair (ER). We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in PROSPERO, was performed. Comparative studies were pooled using random-effects models, and separate single-arm meta-analyses were conducted for OpR and ER. RESULTS: Twenty-six retrospective studies involving 707 patients and 725 procedures were included (574 OpR and 151 ER). Six comparative studies (228 procedures) showed no significant differences between ER and OpR in 30-day mortality (OR, 2.58; 95% CI, 0.53-12.52), 30-day stroke (OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.30-3.91), late stroke, reintervention, or primary patency. In the single-arm analyses, pooled 30-day mortality and stroke rates after OpR were 1.18% and 4.29%, respectively. No 30-day deaths and one stroke were reported after ER, yielding a pooled stroke rate of 1.25% (95% CI, 0.18-8.34). Primary patency was high after both OpR (98.44%) and ER (94.50%). CONCLUSIONS: Observational evidence suggests similar perioperative outcomes and similar observed late event rates for ER and OpR in ECAAs, although heterogeneous follow-up and the absence of time-to-event analyses limit formal comparison of long-term durability. Both approaches were associated with low mortality, stroke, reintervention rates, and excellent primary patency. Open repair remains supported by a larger body of evidence and longer follow-up, whereas evidence for ER remains comparatively limited. Because treatment allocation in the available studies was influenced by patient characteristics, anatomical complexity, and surgical risk, the observed similarity in outcomes should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence. Given the observational design and the predominantly moderate to serious risk of bias of the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in PROSPERO, was performed.

title: SPATIAL ORGANIZATION OF DISTURBED FLOW AFTER CAROTID ENDARTERECTOMY AND CAROTID ARTERY STENTING.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) and carotid artery stenting (CAS) create distinct postoperative geometries. Conventional wall shear stress (WSS)-derived biomarkers quantify disturbed-flow magnitude but not its spatial organisation. We evaluated whether spatial organisation provides complementary haemodynamic information after CEA and CAS. METHODS: In this retrospective, patient-specific computational fluid dynamics study, nine carotid geometries (three healthy, three post-CEA, three post-CAS) were reconstructed from computed tomography angiography. Identical pulsatile boundary conditions were applied to isolate morphological effects. Time-averaged WSS (TAWSS), oscillatory shear index (OSI), relative residence time (RRT), and endothelial cell activation potential (ECAP) were computed. Regions of adverse flow were defined using percentile thresholds (P90, P95, and P99). Spatial organisation was quantified by total area at risk, largest connected hotspot area, hotspot number, and the Spatial Dominance Index (SDI), defined as the largest hotspot area divided by total area at risk. RESULTS: ECAP, OSI, and RRT colocalised with low TAWSS, and spatial descriptors were consistent across biomarkers. Healthy carotids showed the most focal pattern (SDI approximately 0.22; 8-12 hotspots). CEA had the largest total area at risk and largest hotspot but retained relatively high dominance (SDI 0.16-0.17; 48-75 hotspots). The Roadsaver-treated CAS geometries had the smallest total area at risk but the most fragmented pattern, with smaller hotspots and the lowest dominance (SDI 0.09-0.12; 39-70 hotspots). These patterns persisted across P90-P99 thresholds. CONCLUSION: Spatial organisation distinguished carotid revascularisation strategies beyond biomarker magnitude. CEA largely preserved a focal, dominant pattern, whereas the Roadsaver-treated CAS geometries showed fragmented, distributed disturbed flow. The simple, dimensionless SDI may complement established WSS-derived biomarkers in patient-specific haemodynamic assessment.

title: Postoperative complications following carotid endarterectomy are differentially impacted by sex and plaque instability.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to provide novel evidence on the role of sex and plaque instability in post-carotid endarterectomy outcomes. Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for carotid endarterectomy rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing carotid endarterectomy for clinical indications. We performed multivariable binary logistic regression to examine the relationship of biological sex and plaque instability with postoperative outcomes. RESULTS: Data of 394 participants (31% female) were analyzed. Plaque instability was independently associated with decreased odds of hemorrhagic complications at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery, as well as with decreased respiratory complications at 1 year post-surgery. Plaque features accounting for these associations were lipid core, cap infiltration, and plaque inflammation. Female sex was independently associated with increased odds of restenosis at 1 month and 1 year post-surgery. Additionally, females with unstable plaques had more cerebrovascular complications at 1 month than males with unstable plaques, and females with stable plaques had double the odds of any complication at 1 month compared with males with unstable plaques. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings show that sex and plaque instability differentially impact post-endarterectomy outcomes, with males with unstable plaques experiencing the least postoperative complications. Sex and plaque instability may therefore be important factors that play a role in postoperative complications, highlighting their importance in the context of surgical decision-making.

Current clinical guidelines regarding recommendation for carotid endarterectomy rely solely on grade of stenosis and cerebrovascular symptomatology, despite emerging evidence emphasizing the role of sex and plaque instability in determining postoperative outcomes. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of an ongoing cohort study of males and females undergoing carotid endarterectomy for clinical indications.

title: Endovascular Iliac Stenting versus Open Aortobifemoral Bypass for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischaemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative-effectiveness data adjusted for treatment-selection bias remain limited. This multicentre study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD. METHODS: Retrospective, non-randomised cohort study of 171 patients with AIOD (Rutherford 3-6) treated at three centres (UK, Ireland, Egypt) between January 2023 and February 2026. Outcomes were primary patency, freedom from reintervention (FFR), amputation-free survival (AFS), overall survival, and perioperative complications. Cox regression and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for confounding. RESULTS: 125 patients (73.1%) underwent endovascular treatment and 46 (26.9%) open bypass. Endovascular patients were older (66.8 vs 60.8 years, p<0.001) and had a lower burden of TASC C-D disease (53.6% vs 93.5%, p<0.001). Primary patency at 24 months was 62.7% vs 91.8% (log-rank p<0.001; IPTW-adjusted HR 5.67, 95% CI 1.75-18.37). Freedom from reintervention at 24 months was 63.1% vs 93.3% (p<0.001). Amputation-free survival (85.0% vs 87.4%, p=0.992) and overall survival (93.3% vs 90.0%, p=0.335) were comparable between groups. Wound infection was less frequent after endovascular treatment (0.8% vs 10.9%, p=0.006). Major amputation was independently predicted by CLTI presentation (OR 4.0) and age, not treatment group. Progressive infrainguinal disease, rather than failure of proximal revascularisation, accounted for most amputations in both groups. CONCLUSION: Open bypass confers a substantial mid-term patency and reintervention-free survival advantage over endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, most pronounced in TASC D and CLTI subgroups, without a corresponding difference in limb salvage or survival. These findings support risk-stratified rather than uniformly endovascular-first treatment selection, pending confirmation from the ongoing EVOCC randomised trial.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischaemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative-effectiveness data adjusted for treatment-selection bias remain limited. This multicentre study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD.

title: Distinct Temporal Patterns of Limb Loss and Mortality After Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins for No-Option CLTI.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: No-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the most advanced stage of peripheral arterial disease, characterized by exhausted revascularization options and substantial systemic comorbidity. Contemporary registry data have reported amputation-free survival (AFS) as low as approximately 37% at 1 year with standard care alone. Deep venous arterialization (DVA) has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity. Although early trial data have been encouraging, the durability of Transcatheter Arterialization of the Deep Veins (TADV) in routine clinical practice beyond the trial setting remains incompletely defined. We evaluated 2-year technical and clinical outcomes following TADV in a single-center cohort. METHODS: We performed a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 29 consecutive patients with no-option CLTI who underwent TADV, with follow-up extending up to 2 years. Outcomes assessed included technical success, 30-day circuit patency, major amputation, limb salvage, all-cause mortality, and amputation-free survival (AFS). Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate time-to-event outcomes, and univariable Cox regression was used to identify baseline factors associated with AFS and mortality. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all 29 patients (100%). During the follow-up, limb salvage was maintained in 22 of 29 patients (75.9%) (Table 2). The Kaplan-Meier limb-salvage curve plateaued after approximately 7 months, with no major amputations observed among patients who remained amputation-free beyond this point (Figure 1). All-cause mortality was 41.4% (12 of 29 patients) and increased throughout follow-up (Table 2). Older age was significantly associated with mortality (median, 77 vs 71 years; P = .047), and congestive heart failure showed a nonsignificant trend toward increased mortality risk (83.3% vs 47.1%; P = .064) (Table 3). CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of patients with no-option CLTI, TADV achieved durable limb preservation in approximately three-quarters of patients through 2 years of follow-up, with amputation occurring almost exclusively within the first several months after the procedure. All-cause mortality remained substantial throughout follow-up, consistent with the comorbidity burden of this population. These findings support TADV as a limb-salvage option for patients with no-option CLTI who would otherwise face major amputation, although larger multicenter studies are needed to confirm long-term durability.

Deep venous arterialization (DVA) has emerged as a limb-salvage strategy for these patients by arterializing the venous circulation to restore perfusion to the distal extremity.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events (MALE), and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction. OBJECTIVE: To conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluating the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD. METHODS: Following PRISMA/PRISMA-S guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary ROC (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: 2 Ten studies were included. The pooled AUC for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I= 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.855 and specificity 0.836. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than non-registry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; p = 0.004). All models had high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low. CONCLUSIONS: ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to AI reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction.

title: Non-General Anesthesia for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Robustness of Evidence.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for non-general anesthesia (Non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus. Primary outcomes were 30-day and in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications. Random-effects models utilized the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, prediction intervals, and prespecified influence diagnostics. RESULTS: 2 2 Twenty-two studies comprising >150,000 EVAR procedures were analyzed. Non-GA was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality compared with general anesthesia (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.54-1.52; I≈86%; wide prediction interval). Influence diagnostics identified one influential study; its exclusion yielded a lower mortality for Non-GA (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; I≈1%). Non-GA was associated with a modest reduction in hospital LOS (mean difference -0.53 days, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.03), but no consistent differences were observed in ICU stay or major complications. The overall certainty of evidence was judged very low (GRADE). CONCLUSIONS: Non-GA for EVAR does not increase 30-day mortality risk compared to general anesthesia. However, survival estimates are sensitive to study-level characteristics and procedural complexity. Current observational evidence supports individualized anesthetic selection rather than proving superiority or equivalence of either technique.

While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for non-general anesthesia (Non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus.

title: Association between increased superficial calcification clusters in carotid atherosclerosis and cardiovascular events after carotid artery stenting: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on CTA. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n=24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n=96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P= 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P= 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P= 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P= 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P= 0.0256, HR= 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P= 0.0265, HR= 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323). CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.

This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled.

title: Severity-dependent patterns of hemodynamic change in symptomatic carotid stenosis during the waiting period before endarterectomy.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether the rate of hemodynamic change after a symptomatic carotid event differs between moderate and severe stenosis. METHODS: Serial duplex examinations in symptomatic patients awaiting carotid endarterectomy were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model, using an extended, prospectively maintained database. Maximum internal carotid artery peak systolic velocity (ICA PSV) was modeled as a linear function of time from the index event interacting with baseline severity (moderate 125-229, severe ≥230 cm/s), with a random intercept per patient. The rate of change (cm/s per day) and the moderate-severe difference were the principal outcomes. Categorical interval comparisons and paired within-patient changes, including distal common carotid artery (CCA) PSV, were secondary analyses. RESULTS: The time course of maximum ICA PSV differed by baseline severity (interaction p = .006). The modeled rate of change was +1.20 cm/s per day (95% CI 0.28 to 2.12) in moderate and -0.21 cm/s per day (95% CI -0.58 to 0.17) in severe stenosis (difference 1.41 cm/s per day, 95% CI 0.42 to 2.40; p = .005). Secondary analyses were consistent: moderate stenosis accelerated with stable inflow, whereas severe stenosis showed no further ICA acceleration but a fall in distal CCA PSV (-3.0 cm/s; p < .001). CONCLUSION: The rate of hemodynamic change during the waiting period depends on baseline severity: moderate stenosis accelerates, whereas severe stenosis shows little further ICA acceleration, consistent with behavior near a velocity ceiling. Maximum ICA PSV and distal CCA PSV are best read as separate, time-sensitive variables rather than as a single ratio.

title: Outcomes of Open vs Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting. METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into two groups based on the intervention: EVAR vs OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed. RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (OR: 0.25, 95%CI: 0.18-0.34, p<0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95%CI: 0.23-0.42, p<0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95%CI: 0.19-0.31, p<0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (HR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the two treatment modalities.

Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB).

title: Diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert for detecting peripheral arterial disease in people with suspected intermittent claudication referred to secondary care: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Manual ankle-brachial pressure index (ABI) assessment requires significant time and expertise, precluding its use in primary care. Automated vascular assessment tools may offer a simple and efficient alternative for detecting peripheral arterial disease (PAD). However, further evidence is needed before they can be recommended. This study considers the diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert (BVE) in people with suspected intermittent claudication. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional cohort study including people referred to our nurse-led intermittent claudication clinic. BVE measurements were compared to the manual resting ABI/TBI method, using traditional cut-off values of <0.9 and <0.7, respectively. RESULTS: 217 participants and 430 limbs were included, with an overall PAD prevalence of 46%. Sensitivity, specificity, positive (PPV) and negative predictor values (NPV) for the BVE were 88.5%, 80.7%, 81.3% and 88.1% respectively, when compared to the manual ABI. When compared to the manual TBI, the sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV for the BVE were 45.5%, 88%, 62.5% and 78.6% respectively, though this analysis included only 38 limbs. No BVE diagnoses were based on ABI alone, 71% were based on waveform alone and 29% were based on a combination of ABI and waveform. The BVE assessment was significantly quicker to perform than the manual method (p<0.01). CONCLUSION: The BVE demonstrated favourable sensitivity and specificity for detecting or excluding PAD compared to the manual ABI. Further work is needed comparing this device to others, across a range of clinical populations and settings before it can be considered in routine clinical practice.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Exploratory Haemodynamic Numerical Simulation of Patients with Multichannelled Aortic Dissection: A Multicentre, Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Multichannelled aortic dissection (MCAD) is a rare type of aortic dissection with limited data on its clinical features and outcomes. This multicentre, retrospective cohort study compared clinical outcomes between MCAD and double channelled aortic dissection (DCAD) and explored haemodynamic differences. METHODS: Patients with aortic dissection were enrolled from three tertiary hospitals. Patients with one true lumen and one false lumen were classified as having DCAD, whereas those with one true lumen and multiple false lumina were classified as having MCAD. Propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were 30 day and five year all cause mortality after diagnosis. Secondary outcomes included preprocedural mortality, aortic dissection related mortality, post-operative complications, and re-intervention. Overall survival was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Haemodynamic differences were evaluated by exploratory computational fluid dynamics (CFD) analysis. RESULTS: After matching, 50 patients were included in each group (n = 100). The difference in 30 day mortality was significant (p = .046) and largely reflected preprocedural deaths, which occurred in six patients with MCAD (12%) and none with DCAD (p = .027). Overall survival differed between groups (log rank p = .037; hazard ratio 2.72, 95% confidence interval 1.03 - 7.18; p = .044). Kaplan-Meier estimated mortality at 30 days, one year, and five years was 16%, 23%, and 29% in MCAD compared with 4%, 8%, and 12% in DCAD, respectively. Among treated patients, re-intervention was more frequent in MCAD than in DCAD (21% vs. 6%; p = .036), whereas post-operative complication rates did not differ. Exploratory CFD analysis suggested greater false lumen haemodynamic burden in MCAD. CONCLUSION: MCAD was associated with greater preprocedural mortality and more frequent re-intervention than DCAD. These findings may identify MCAD as a higher risk phenotype warranting closer surveillance and timely evaluation. Haemodynamic observations remain exploratory and require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

This multicentre, retrospective cohort study compared clinical outcomes between MCAD and double channelled aortic dissection (DCAD) and explored haemodynamic differences. METHODS: Patients with aortic dissection were enrolled from three tertiary hospitals.

title: Endoscopic versus open great saphenous vein harvesting for lower extremity arterial bypass: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare postoperative outcomes of patients undergoing lower extremity arterial bypass (LEAB) for peripheral artery disease (PAD) with endoscopic great saphenous vein harvest (EVH) versus open vein harvest (OVH), and to investigate the impact of publication year on bypass patency. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through January 2025 for comparative studies of EVH versus OVH in LEAB. Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analysed using Cox proportional hazards models. Binary and continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses by publication year (≤2015 vs >2015) were performed to explore temporal trends in patency. RESULTS: 2 Thirteen retrospective cohort studies comprising 12 401 patients were included. EVH was associated with higher risk of primary patency loss compared with OVH (HR 1.32; 95% CI 1.04-1.68; p=.030) and a borderline longer operative time (MD 58.98 minutes; 95% CI 0.63-117.32; p=.050; I=96%), but significantly lower wound complications (RR 0.68; 95% CI 0.57-0.80; p<.001). No differences were observed in primary-assisted patency, secondary patency, length of stay, major amputation, limb salvage, or mortality. Subgroup analysis showed that the primary patency disadvantage was driven by studies published up to 2015 (HR 1.49; p=.010), with no significant difference in studies published after 2015 (HR 0.97; p=.900), although the interaction test was not significant (p=.100). Meta-regression did not demonstrate an association between publication year and primary patency effect size (p=.890). CONCLUSION: EVH significantly reduces wound complications but is associated with lower primary patency and potentially longer operative times compared with OVH, disadvantages that do not translate into differences in secondary patency, limb salvage, major amputation, or mortality. Further prospective studies are needed to define the role of EVH to better inform LEAB operative planning.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through January 2025 for comparative studies of EVH versus OVH in LEAB. Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analysed using Cox proportional hazards models.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Transperitoneal vs Retroperitoneal Approaches of Open Aortic Repair for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Stratified by the Iliac Bifurcation Involvement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared to OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study aims to compare the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by the iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting. METHODS: The SVS Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery (CIA) bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses, as well as a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), were performed. RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA, and 1,791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared to RPA, TPA was associated with higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.05-1.49, p=0.011), MACE (OR: 1.26, 95%CI: 1.11-1.44, p=0.001), and a lower 1-year survival rate (HR: 1.23, 95%CI: 1.09-1.39, p=0.001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of lower extremity (LE) ischemia (OR: 0.47, 95%CI: 0.25-0.91, p=0.024) without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR: 0.80, 95%CI: 0.42-1.51, p=0.485), MACE (OR: 0.86, 95%CI: 0.52-1.42, p=0.563), and 1-year survival (HR: 0.93, 95%CI: 0.59-1.47, p=0.768). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, involvement of the iliac bifurcation in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. Whereas for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with lower odds of LE ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared to OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) non-thoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with non-thoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with < 2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.
englishSummary: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts.

title: Progress on the related mechanisms of vascular calcification in autogenous arteriovenous fistula in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for end-stage renal disease patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis as a replacement therapy. As the duration of dialysis increases, the risk of vascular access-related complications such as AVF stenosis, thrombosis, vascular calcification (VC), and aneurysm formation gradually rises. Among these, VC has been proven to be independently associated with the occurrence and mortality of cardiovascular diseases in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). VC in the AVF of dialysis patients can lead to AVF failure, severely limiting its usability and increasing the risk of mortality among dialysis patients. Unlike previous reviews that predominantly focused on isolated mechanisms such as mineral metabolism or arterial calcification, this narrative review innovatively integrates the crosstalk among hemodynamic stress, inflammation, oxidative stress, deficiency of endogenous calcification inhibitors and pathological matrix remodeling, thereby providing a multidimensional perspective on AVF-VC. This review reframes the current understanding of AVF-VC, shifting it from a generalized complication of CKD-mineral and bone disorder to a distinct, fistula-specific pathological entity. This conceptual advancement offers a theoretical foundation for developing precision intervention strategies tailored to the unique microenvironment of the AVF.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: n n This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp ( = 261) or MHCA ( = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: p p The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications.

title: Estrogen hormonal therapy is not associated with increased risk of venous thrombosis in total hip arthroplasty or hemiarthroplasty for femoral neck fractures.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of estrogen hormone therapy on venous thrombotic events for femoral neck fractures treated with either total hip arthroplasty (THA) or hemiarthroplasty (HA). DESIGN: Retrospective cohort analysis. SETTING: TriNetX Health Research Network. PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients who sustained a femoral neck fracture (OTA/AO 31B) between 2005 and 2025 who were treated with either THA or HA were categorized into groups based on whether they were prescribed systemic estrogen hormone therapy (EHT) within 3 months before or after their fracture. OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcomes were deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) within 3 months after their fracture. A matched cohort was created after a 1:1 propensity match for demographics, diabetes, obesity, and tobacco use. Measures of association models were used to determine odds ratios. RESULTS: P P A total of 39,631 patients with femoral neck fractures treated with either a THA or HA were identified. Of these, 330 (0.8%) patients with femoral neck fractures were prescribed estrogen within 3 months before or after their fracture. After a matched cohort comparison, there were no statistically significant differences in rates of PE (odds ratio [OR] = 1.31; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-3.03;= 0.525) or for DVT (OR = 1.67; 95% CI, 0.78-3.61;= 0.184). CONCLUSION: Systemic EHT was not associated with a significantly increased risk of DVT or PE after operatively treated femoral neck fractures with THA or HA. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, Prognostic.

title: Functional connectivity recovers canine-human network homology along the evolutionary cortical hierarchy.
abstract: ≈ p = 0.002 p > 0.3 p = 0.93 Mapping functional brain organization between species is a prerequisite for translating connectivity biomarkers from animal models to patients, but connectivity-based correspondence has been demonstrated almost exclusively in primates. We tested whether canine-human network homology can be recovered from functional connectivity alone, using only five network-level anatomical priors, and benchmarked a spectral manifold alignment framework (Laplacian-eigenmap embedding with Procrustes alignment on network centroids) against a simple connectivity-signature matching baseline. Data comprised resting-state fMRI from 15 canines with endovascular permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pre-occlusion baseline and hyperacute post-occlusion sessions) and two public OpenNeuro datasets: 29 chronic-phase post-stroke aphasia patients scanned before and after rehabilitation (ds003999) and 10 healthy controls (ds000224). Held-out canine-human network homologies were recovered well above chance (top-5 network correspondence up to 54.5% vs. permutation null18%,), and correspondence followed the evolutionary cortical hierarchy: visual and somatomotor homologies were recovered several-fold above chance, default-mode only weakly-extending a gradient previously described in primates to a carnivore. Notably, simple signature matching (54.5%) outperformed manifold alignment (35.5%), indicating that the homology signal is strong enough to be captured without embedding machinery at translational cohort sizes. Within species, canine network metrics showed no treatment-arm differences (all), and chronic-phase patients did not differ from controls in modularity (); a sensitivity analysis bounds these nulls. All results are fully reproducible from shared code and public data.

title: Surgical, endovascular, and systemic management of renal cell carcinoma with intravascular recurrence.
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) recurrence within the vasculature represents a rare and challenging clinical scenario with limited evidence to guide management. We report a patient with clear cell RCC and level 4 IVC thrombus who underwent successful radical nephrectomy with IVC thrombectomy and subsequently developed disease recurrence in the supradiaphragmatic IVC and pulmonary arteries. Multidisciplinary management included novel endovascular removal of the recurrent IVC tumor followed by pulmonary bilobectomy for progressive tumor emboli. The patient remains without evidence of recurrent disease. This case highlights the complex multidisciplinary decision-making and potential role of minimally invasive endovascular techniques in managing intravascular RCC.

title: A method for expressing two proteins at a tunable ratio allows for studying the kinetics of creatine transport by MCT12.
abstract: M Interactions between physically or functionally coupled proteins are often studied by co-expression from the same or separate plasmids, but protein ratios can vary widely between individual cells. To overcome this limitation, we developed a strategy to generate tunable and constant expression ratios using a single vector encoding two proteins separated by a P2A site followed by short AAA codon repeats that progressively reduce ribosomal readthrough. After validating this approach with the fluorescent proteins eGFP and mCherry, we applied it to characterize the transport cycle of the electroneutral monocarboxylate transporter MCT12, a task that is otherwise difficult to achieve experimentally. By co-expressing MCT12 with the concentrative creatine transporter CRT1 at defined ratios, we were able to determine the substrate turnover rate of MCT12 and its substrate K. This approach enables precise control of protein stoichiometry, facilitating quantitative mechanistic studies of interacting proteins in cells.

title: Combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches for embolization of a traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistula with concomitant middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula.
abstract: Endovascular treatment (EVT) is a useful modality for traumatic carotid‑cavernous fistulas (CCFs); in rare cases, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches may be applied for embolization of the fistula with concomitant internal carotid artery (ICA) sacrifice and preservation of the ophthalmic artery (OphA). A 62‑year‑old female patient sustained a motor vehicle accident and developed proptosis, chemosis, and congestion in her right eye, while no abnormalities in ocular motility or visual acuity were noted. Computed tomography angiography confirmed the CCF. Under general anesthesia, digital subtraction angiography revealed a right CCF supplied antegradely by the ICA and retrogradely by the posterior communicating artery (PcomA). A left middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was identified. Access to the basilar artery was established. A microcatheter was retrogradely navigated via the PcomA to reach the proximal ICA across the fistula. Then, another microcatheter was advanced into the cavernous sinus via an antegrade ICA approach. Subsequently, combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial coiling with ICA sacrifice for the CCF was successfully performed. During coiling, the patency of the OphA was monitored through the PcomA microcatheter. Afterwards, the middle meningeal arteriovenous fistula was embolized. At the 1‑month follow‑up, her right eye redness and swelling resolved, and at the 3‑month follow‑up, she had recovered well and returned to her normal status. Therefore, when embolizing the CCF with ICA sacrifice, if the PcomA is well‑developed, the combined antegrade and retrograde transarterial approaches can be used, which may facilitate the obliteration of the CCF and preservation of the OphA.

title: A thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor: A case report.
abstract: Thoracic SWI/SNF-related BAF chromatin remodeling complex subunit ATPase 4 (SMARCA4)-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a newly recognized, high-grade malignant neoplasm that is rare in clinical practice. There is no standardized or clearly defined treatment protocol for SMARCA4-UT in clinical guidelines. The current study reports the case of a 54-year-old male patient who presented with a 2-month history of an intermittent productive cough. Bronchoscopy demonstrated a neoplasm in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe bronchus, which almost obstructed the lumen, with a hypervascular surface, suggestive of a right upper lobe carcinoma. Histopathological examination confirmed a poorly differentiated carcinoma. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a SMARCA4 gene mutation in exon 4, classifying the tumor as SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated lung carcinoma. The patient developed superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS), requiring emergent percutaneous stent placement. Treatment also included computed tomography-guided cryoablation and radiofrequency ablation (RFA), alongside targeted molecular therapy with crizotinib. Despite aggressive multimodal therapy, the patient succumbed to tumor thrombosis at 1 month post-treatment. Overall, SMARCA4-UT is rare and diagnostically challenging, lacking standardized treatment guidelines. In clinical practice, cryoablation with argon-helium and RFA may provide palliative benefits by alleviating tumor burden and improving quality of life. Endovascular intervention provides a rapid and effective approach to alleviate tumor-induced SVCS. However, subsequent anticoagulation and antineoplastic therapies require further investigation to determine their efficacy in the management of such cases.

The current study reports the case of a 54-year-old male patient who presented with a 2-month history of an intermittent productive cough.

title: Meta-analysis of the histopathological features of surgically removed aortas classified according to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents.
abstract: The Society for Cardiovascular Pathology (SCVP) and the Association for European Cardiovascular Pathology (AECVP) published consensus statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta to unify nomenclature and provide a new classification scheme to systematically evaluate the degenerative and inflammatory lesions of the thoracic aorta. The aim of this meta-analysis was to determine the histopathological features of thoracic aneurysmatic aortas, thoracic dissected aortas, and thoracic aortas in patients with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Additionally, the aim was to map how consensus documents and classification schemes is used in practice and research. Articles for analysis were identified while searching for references to the SCVP and AECVP consensus documents, resulting in 174 articles. After applying the exclusion and inclusion criteria, 10 articles were included in the analysis. Four cohorts were analysed: the whole cohort, the aneurysm cohort, the dissection cohort, and the BAV cohort. Medial degeneration was found in all cohorts. The dissection cohort showed more severe medial degeneration than the aneurysm cohort or the BAV cohort. The BAV cohort showed the mildest medial degeneration compared to the other cohorts. More prevalent smooth muscle cell nuclei loss was linked to dissection. The BAV cohort showed milder changes in elastic fibers. Atherosclerosis was comparable among all cohorts. Medial degeneration represents the pathological process of several aortic diseases. All studied components of medial degeneration were present in aneurysms, dissections, and BAV aortas. The consensus documents have been useful tools and assist with the systematic evaluation of resected aortas, although their use in the complexity is limited.
